content.value: PDS Wave 17 — Boot the Scratch Target and Re-Fire: the crown is one clean run from its seal

Living wave Paper for wave 17 of the Personal Development Server epic (root task pds-w1-crown-proof; wave task task-cdff5b4cd01c15d9). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-pds-charter.md (PDS-D1..D241). This Paper is the wave's living story — Digest appends the survey digest before the verifiers fly, Decide appends the wave plan before the builders fly, Review closes it as the debrief. Fan-out workers never write this Paper; each Fable phase folds their bp-task reports in.

STATUS: SURVEYING. One Fable strategized and opened this Paper; 16 Sonnet surveyors are casting a wide net over the boot mechanic, the free-reuse fence, rung 6's health, and the collection path. The phase markers below are preserved as written so the wave's story stays readable end to end.
The wish, verbatim in substance

MODEL CONSTRAINT (hard): Fable 5 is spend-limited — every phase runs on Opus/Sonnet, and Decide MUST set builder_model='opus' for EVERY slice, never 'fable'. THIS CYCLE: PDS WAVE 17 — BOOT THE SCRATCH TARGET AND RE-FIRE. The crown climb FIRED for real in wave 16: a 1.4 GB export was taken, 5 rungs PASSED against live production, 0 FAILED, and six aborted on ONE missing local prerequisite. The expensive part is already paid — the parked bundle is reusable, so the re-fire costs ZERO attempts. Root task: pds-w1-crown-proof.
What actually landed — reconciling the charter with the ledger

The crown proof (pds-w1-crown-proof) reads 9/12. Criteria 0-5 and 7-9 are MET; unmet are 6, 10, 11. Criterion 6 is the content-and-presence reboot-convergence rung; 10 is the merge event the LEAD closes; 11 is the single-run attribution fence. The nine met criteria are the wave-2..7 mosaic — and that is precisely the problem criterion 11 exists to forbid.

WAVE 13 (Fire the Climb, C+): the climb DID NOT FIRE. Not a refusal on the merits and not a defect — the box never offered a qualifying draw, and then the builder's turn was CUT at poll 3 of 30 with the poller inside the reclaimed worktree. The wave's own finding: a fire must SURVIVE its launcher — detach it from the agent turn. Four instruments landed; net crown movement zero.

WAVE 16 (the trigger, task-cdff5b4cd01c15d9): the fire SURVIVED its launcher this time — armed detached, agent returned, the launcher ran the REAL frozen harness (pds-pull-proof.sh), DRAW 1 cleared (mem_mib=2578, floor=2200, builds empty, verdict=FIRE), and a REAL full export was taken: /tmp/pds-full-export/full-default.tar, 1,405,095,424 bytes, served_sha 8eeaf688fff03986da63e54bfc5cb323b53c165d, run_id 1b515ee5, attempt 4 of 5. Outcome: 5 PASS, 6 ABORT, 0 FAIL, rc=2. Its own transcript refuses to overclaim: 'This is the honest partial artifact the wave is supposed to carry; it is NOT a green.'

WHY WAVE 16 ABORTED SIX RUNGS — and it is NOT an engine failure: env:scratch-target-not-booted. /tmp/pds-w14.1b515ee5/scratch.env was absent, so there was no Repo for the sentinels, and rungs 0c/1/2/4/5/6 all aborted on that single missing local prerequisite. WHAT PASSED, all re-derived live against production (deployed sha 8eeaf688): 0a source pinned + dev dialect LIVE (73951232 bytes, 18 members); 0b deployed sha EQUALS the worktree the target migrated from; 3 the type deny cascades at ROW grain (0 ticket rows DEV, 1 FULL); 7 the source REFUSES a merge import (HTTP 403 bundle_import_disabled); 8 the source did not move under the run (uptime 123 -> 302, monotonic). ZERO rungs FAILED.

PRODUCTION WAS UNHARMED — measured after the export, not assumed: GET /api/schemas -> HTTP 200 in 0.14s; MemAvailable 1931 MiB; dmesg 'out of memory' lines: 0. The streaming spill engine carried a 1.4 GB export against the live content API with no incident.

blocks.title: The engine is proven safe at 1.4 GB

content.value: The economics inverted: the expensive part is already paid

acquire_full_bundle's PDS-D20 provenance gate REUSES the parked bundle when its served_sha matches the live source. Measured by the lead after wave 16: full-default.tar.meta served_sha = 8eeaf688...; guerrilla HEAD over SSH = 8eeaf688... MATCH. So the parked 1.4 GB bundle is REUSABLE and a re-fire spends 0 of the remaining attempt. This INVERTS the risk calculus every prior wave operated under — the scarce, expensive, dangerous part is ALREADY PAID. But guerrilla auto-deploys on merge (~58x/24h); if it has redeployed since 11:58Z the sha moves and reuse is REFUSED. Re-verify at FIRE time; if it moved, SAY SO rather than assuming, and recompute the budget as spent+2 (PDS-D224, never a literal).
The direction: The Booted Fire

ONE serial --all climb, fired DETACHED, into a scratch target PROVEN booted into the harness's own RUN_TAG-derived home before the arm, reusing the already-paid 1.4 GB bundle (re-verified live at fire time), greening rungs 0-9 INCLUDING the historically-hard rung 6 with its leg-B guard control FIRING, under ONE run_id. Then this Paper names the single remaining step to the seal: 10 (the LEAD merges the pushed fire record) and 11 (re-stamp 0-9 with that run_id, verify all eleven ids identical, stamp 11 last and alone).

The finished experience: a developer reads ONE transcript that opens with the honesty banner (the sha guerrilla actually served, which plane, the run's own measured RSS peak), climbs 0a/0b/0c/1/2/3/4/5/6/7/8 in one process, prints the unqualified full-ladder PASS line (which PDS-D236 proves a partial invocation structurally cannot emit), and ends with a summary roster naming every rung PASS under one run_id. That transcript is the crown. Everything after it — merge, re-stamp, fence-verify — is bookkeeping the Paper spells out so the seal is one clear step, not a mystery.

What matters most now, in order: (1) BOOT the scratch target into the harness's RUN_TAG home and PROVE scratch.env exists and the Repo answers BEFORE arming — this is the exact prerequisite wave 16 missed. (2) Pre-warm MIX_ENV=prod BEFORE the timed window so a 155s cold compile is not mistaken for a hang, with CC=/usr/bin/clang (the ~/.local/bin/cc trap). (3) Re-verify the parked bundle's served_sha against live guerrilla at fire time; record reuse-confirmed or the refusal. (4) Tighten the LAUNCHER draw gate via PDS_LAUNCH_MEM_FLOOR_MIB to cover the 2235.43 MiB measured demand, leaving PDS_FULL_EXPORT_MIN_MEM_MB UNSET so the frozen harness floor stays 2200 and the transcript carries NO asterisk. (5) Arm DETACHED — the slice records pid + transcript path and RETURNS, it MUST NOT POLL. (6) COLLECT is the LEAD's, never the agent that fired.

ZERO NEW SCRIPTS. Every instrument is merged: pds-crown-launch.sh (launcher, not frozen), pds-pull-proof.sh (FROZEN — quote the blob via git rev-parse e219e97cc, never shasum), pds-export-peak-measure.sh, pds-idle-sampler.sh, pds-scratch-target.sh, pds-crown-stamp.sh. A proposed new .sh is the recession five waves died of and is refused on sight. Permitted new artifacts: a fire RECORD, a TRANSCRIPT, a DERIVATION output, charter/Paper text. FENCE: scripts/pds-* ONLY — do NOT touch tooling/grip/, cloud/, or api/**.
Carrying wave 16's safety finding forward

The harness floor of 2200 sits 35.43 MiB BELOW the export's own measured incremental demand (rss_peak 2483304 kB - baseline 194228 kB = 2235.43 MiB; MiB = kB/1024 never /1000). A draw clearing at exactly 2200 does not have the memory to finish. Wave 16's answer was correct and asterisk-free: tighten the LAUNCHER's draw gate via PDS_LAUNCH_MEM_FLOOR_MIB (the launcher explicitly sanctions 'the floor may be TIGHTENED, never loosened') while leaving PDS_FULL_EXPORT_MIN_MEM_MB UNSET so the frozen harness floor stays 2200 and the transcript carries NO asterisk. Never lower a floor except by derivation against the DEPLOYED engine.
Naming the seal: what criteria 10 and 11 need after a clean 0-9 green

Criterion 10 (PR merged, LEAD closes — MERGE-GATED, PDS-D163): NOT to be stamped until rungs 3 and 4 are GREEN in the transcript of the wave that pays it (3 and 4 read off the ONE full bundle; 1/2/5/6 against a real booted target; every rung passing WITH its controls FIRING), and then only by the LEAD on an actual merge to main. The fire RECORD + TRANSCRIPT are pushed (wave 16's reviewer pushed #5424 — that is the new normal); the LEAD merges and stamps 10. HAZARD: cmux_hook.go:193-237 closes this task UNCONDITIONALLY on the next Stop event once every criterion reads met — the PDS-D138 false close, which already fired once on this exact task. Criterion 11's presence is what blocks that silent auto-close.

Criterion 11 (SINGLE-RUN ATTRIBUTION FENCE): every one of criteria 0-10 must cite ONE IDENTICAL RUN_ID, and that run must be the run whose full bundle actually existed. TO SATISFY: (a) re-prove criteria 0-10 from ONE serial climb and stamp each with that run's id in the evidence, or (b) explicitly REFUSE the crown, naming the rung that failed. The LEAD verifies the eleven run ids are identical before this is marked met — it is NEVER stamped by a builder alongside the rung it just ran, and it is stamped LAST and ALONE. Stamp discipline: criterion text is NEVER typed inline (criterion 6 carries literal backticks the shell executes as command substitution; 5/6/11 carry single quotes) — fetch to a file, pass by "$(cat f)"; evidence TERSE against the ~9-11 KB request-line ceiling.

THE OPEN QUESTION THE SURVEY MUST SETTLE: does reusing wave 16's parked 1.4 GB bundle (served_sha still matching) satisfy criterion 11's clause 'that run must be the run whose full bundle actually existed'? Under PDS-D236 attribution is process-level — one --all invocation emits one summary roster citing the new run_id for every rung. If reuse satisfies the fence, the crown is FREE. If the fence demands a freshly-minted bundle under the new run_id, the wave spends the remaining attempt on a fresh export. Either way the wave completes; the reuse only makes it cheaper. This is the load-bearing assumption, and it is survey question 2.
Direction debate: the rivals weighed

RIVAL A — Boot and fire (the lead's literal directive): one slice that boots the scratch target, proves scratch.env, re-verifies bundle reuse, arms the launcher detached, returns without polling. Minimal, surgical; the whole wave is one builder slice plus the LEAD's collection. Virtue: matches the wish exactly and spends nothing. Risk: a bare re-fire may abort on the NEXT unmodeled local prerequisite — exactly the shape wave 16 died of.

RIVAL B — Boot, fire, AND harden the boot so it cannot abort again: recognize that the ladder's LOCAL prerequisites (scratch Repo, full-bundle availability) have failed to line up under one run across MULTIPLE waves (wave 9 aborted 3/4 on full-export-unavailable; wave 16 aborted 6 rungs on scratch-not-booted). Invest in a PRE-ARM checklist that PROVES all of rungs 0-9's local prerequisites green before spending the arm. Virtue: makes the fire near-deterministic. Risk: reads as 'file another instrument', the recession five waves died of.

RIVAL C — Sequence the boot INTO the launcher: the deeper issue is that boot-the-scratch-target is a MANUAL step separate from the launcher, forgotten or mis-homed every wave. Edit pds-crown-launch.sh (NOT frozen — only pds-pull-proof.sh is) so it boots the scratch target into its OWN RUN_TAG-derived home before invoking the harness. Zero new scripts. Virtue: the boot can never be forgotten again. Risk: a launcher edit under time pressure that mis-wires BARKPARK_HOME could strand the very run it means to save.

WHY THE WINNER WON — A executed with B's discipline, C's durability folded in only if the seam demands it. The lead is right that the wave's success condition is THE TRANSCRIPT and that is narrow. But 'boot the scratch target and PROVE scratch.env exists before arming' IS the pre-arm-checklist insight — the lead's own sequence step (1) is literally that. So the winner is Rival A run with a proven (not assumed) pre-arm checklist using the EXISTING instruments, and a launcher-boot integration (C) ONLY if the survey finds the BARKPARK_HOME flow between launcher, scratch-target and harness cannot otherwise be made consistent around the RUN_TAG-derived path. We do not file a fifth instrument; we make the boot a proven precondition of the one shot.

THE SHARPEST ATTACK ON THE WINNER, and how the wave absorbs it: the 'free re-fire' premise may be the very thing that fails the fence — if criterion 11 demands the full bundle be produced UNDER the wave-17 run_id, reusing wave 16's bytes means rungs 3/4 ran against bytes not minted by this run, a hidden mosaic between wave 16's export and wave 17's dev-pull. ABSORPTION: this becomes survey question 2 (read acquire_full_bundle's reuse guard, criterion 11's exact text, and PDS-D236's attribution mechanism). Under D236 attribution is process-level: one process runs all rungs and emits one roster citing the new run_id, and the reuse guard's served_sha == live check IS the D20 freshness proof. So reuse most plausibly satisfies the fence. BUT if the survey finds the fence demands a fresh mint, the wave spends the remaining attempt (budget allows spent+2 = two fires). Re-verifying at fire time and RECORDING reuse-confirmed-or-refused is therefore a hard criterion on the fire slice, not an optimization.

SECOND ATTACK: the scratch boot OOMs or takes 155s cold and the fire slice mistakes it for a hang, or chases it into the frozen harness. ABSORPTION: budget the ~3.5 min cold compile; pre-warm MIX_ENV=prod BEFORE the timed window (PDS-D241) with CC=/usr/bin/clang; redirect boot output to a file, never pipe to tail (PDS-D34 trap 4 hangs forever); local API boot has OOMed before — budget for it, do not mistake an OOM for a hang, do not chase it into the harness. THIRD ATTACK: can ONE --all invocation green rungs 3+4 (full bundle) AND 6 (reboot convergence) AND all dev-pull rungs together? Precedent says yes: wave 7's --all got 10 PASS / 1 FAIL in one process (only rung 6 failed); wave 16's abort was purely the missing scratch.env. Rung 6 is the historically-flaky one and is survey question 4.
The survey plan: 16 Sonnet surveyors, wide net
Width is cheap now; the Digest phase distills. Each question names suspected files, claims to check, and how the answer changes the plan.

1. boot-flow — How BARKPARK_HOME / PDS_SCRATCH_POINTER flow from pds-crown-launch.sh (RUN_ID -> RUN_TAG) into pds-scratch-target.sh up --verify and into pds-pull-proof.sh rung 0c. Does the harness boot the scratch target itself, or expect a pre-booted target in $BARKPARK_HOME? Where must the boot be inserted so scratch.env exists when rung 0c runs? THE load-bearing mechanic — wave 16 aborted here.

2. reuse-fence — Read acquire_full_bundle's served_sha reuse guard, criterion 11's exact text, and PDS-D236's attribution mechanism. Does reusing wave 16's parked bundle under a fresh run_id satisfy 'the run whose full bundle actually existed'? Does the rung 3/4 transcript line cite the run's id on reuse? Load-bearing.

3. bundle-state — Current /tmp/pds-full-export state: attempts file value, budget, full-default.tar.meta served_sha (8eeaf688) vs live guerrilla HEAD RIGHT NOW (SSH + /status.json). If moved, reuse refused -> recompute PDS-D224 spent+2 budget. Is attempts=4, budget=5, one attempt left?

4. rung6-health — On the current sha, is the visibility split still 31 private / 3 public in rung 6's scope, do command/paper/task still declare public, does leg B (PDS_STEP6_GUARD_DEMO=1) fire, what is the Bootstrap SKIP count vs the separate TagRegistry line (PDS-D145)? Wave 7 rung 6 FAILED ('THE CONTROL DID NOT FIRE') and wave 9 PASSED — is it healthy now?

5. launcher-commit — Is pds-crown-launch.sh committed to main / scripts/? It appears only under /private/tmp worktrees, not in scripts/. Where is the canonical copy, are the copies identical, and is editing it (to integrate the boot, Rival C) permitted under the freeze (only pds-pull-proof.sh is frozen)?

6. harness-freeze — Does THIS worktree's scripts/pds-pull-proof.sh match the frozen blob e219e97ccf7f33797c86a2b84d998d599b6bda31 via git rev-parse (never shasum)? Which worktree is suitable to fire from (the primary checkout is UNSUITABLE per PDS-D241)?

7. draw-gate — pds-crown-launch.sh's draw gate: how PDS_LAUNCH_MEM_FLOOR_MIB is read, the build-idle predicate (bp-site-build-* running listing EMPTY, PDS-D227), current MemAvailable + build activity on this host. What value should PDS_LAUNCH_MEM_FLOOR_MIB take to cover 2235.43 MiB while leaving the 2200 harness floor untouched?

8. detached-arm — Exactly how wave 16 armed the launcher detached (nohup/setsid/background), recorded pid + transcript path, and returned without polling. Map the precise invocation and the record format so the fire slice reproduces it. Wave 13 died to agent-turn length with a poller in-turn — the detach is non-negotiable.

9. coldboot-oom — State of api/_build/prod in candidate fire worktrees (ABSENT -> 155.72s prod compile per the wave-13 review). How to pre-warm MIX_ENV=prod with CC=/usr/bin/clang before the timed window. What does an OOM during boot look like vs a hang, and how to not chase it into the harness?

10. mosaic-map — For each of criteria 0-9 on pds-w1-crown-proof, which run_id (if any) does its current evidence cite? Confirm the fence gap: only criterion 0 names a run (20260720T032558Z-28651), and it is stale in substance (deployed sha moved). This is the re-stamp target list.

11. stamp-recipe — Read pds-crown-stamp.sh + pds-crown-stamp-recipe.md. How to re-stamp criteria 0-9 with a fresh run_id, the criterion-11-last-and-alone protocol, the backtick/single-quote escaping traps (criteria 5/6/11), the ~9-11 KB request-line ceiling, and the stale-claim-epoch rejection (bp task pulse bumps the epoch). Note: bp task claim is BROKEN ('unresolved placeholder :doc_id') — claim via HTTP POST /v1/data/mutate/production.

12. autoclose-hazard — cmux_hook.go:193-237: how the false-close fires on a Stop event once every criterion reads met, how criterion 11's presence blocks it, and what the LEAD must watch when stamping 10 so the crown does not close silently on a mosaic.

13. collection-protocol — What exactly does the LEAD do to collect a fire (read transcript, verify the unqualified full-ladder PASS roster, re-stamp 0-9, merge, stamp 10, verify eleven ids, stamp 11)? Map from wave 16's collection task (task-cdff5b4cd01c15d9) and prior collections so the hand-off is unambiguous.

14. prior-papers — Read pds-wave-13-2026-07-21 and any wave 14/15 paper/debrief. What exactly went wrong at each fire attempt (wave 13 agent-turn cut; wave 15 pointed at a probe stub not the real harness; wave 16 scratch-not-booted)? Extract the recurring root cause so wave 17 does not repeat it.

15. concurrent-fence — Are the concurrent cycles (tooling/grip truth-grip w7, cloud/ console-hardening w4, felix-pristine on api/**) touching anything the fire needs, and is the build storm on this host right now going to depress the floor below the tightened gate at fire time? Map the fence collisions and the current bp-site-build-* cadence.

16. migration-parity — Rung 0b asserts guerrilla's deployed sha is an ancestor of the worktree the scratch target migrated from (merge-base --is-ancestor). Current guerrilla deployed sha vs the fire worktree HEAD; will 0b pass at fire time, or is the box ahead of the fire worktree (a PDS-D78 deploy-epoch event, not an assertion to loosen)?
In flight now

Surveying. 16 Sonnet surveyors dispatched. Next: Digest folds their reports into this Paper and designs the verify fleet BEFORE the verifiers fly. Then Decide appends the wave plan (one boot-and-fire builder slice, opus, plus the seal-naming) BEFORE the builders fly. Then the fire, detached; then the LEAD collects; then Review closes this Paper as the debrief.

Criterion 11's presence is what blocks that silent auto-close.

Criterion 11 (SINGLE-RUN ATTRIBUTION FENCE): every one of criteria 0-10 must cite ONE IDENTICAL RUN_ID, and that run must be the run whose full bundle actually existed. TO SATISFY: (a) re-prove criteria 0-10 from ONE serial climb and stamp each with that run's id in the evidence, or (b) explicitly REFUSE the crown, naming the rung that failed. The LEAD verifies the eleven run ids are identical before this is marked met — it is NEVER stamped by a builder alongside the rung it just ran, and it is stamped LAST and ALONE. Stamp discipline: criterion text is NEVER typed inline (criterion 6 carries literal backticks the shell executes as command substitution; 5/6/11 carry single quotes) — fetch to a file, pass by "$(cat f)"; evidence TERSE against the ~9-11 KB request-line ceiling.

The load-bearing assumption THE OPEN QUESTION THE SURVEY MUST SETTLE: does reusing wave 16's parked 1.4 GB bundle (served_sha still matching) satisfy criterion 11's clause 'that run must be the run whose full bundle actually existed'? Under PDS-D236 attribution is process-level — one --all invocation emits one summary roster citing the new run_id for every rung. If reuse satisfies the fence, the crown is FREE. If the fence demands a freshly-minted bundle under the new run_id, the wave spends the remaining attempt on a fresh export. Either way the wave completes; the reuse only makes it cheaper. This is the load-bearing assumption, and it is survey question 2.

Direction debate: the rivals weighed

RIVAL A — Boot and fire (the lead's literal directive): one slice that boots the scratch target, proves scratch.env, re-verifies bundle reuse, arms the launcher detached, returns without polling. Minimal, surgical; the whole wave is one builder slice plus the LEAD's collection. Virtue: matches the wish exactly and spends nothing. Risk: a bare re-fire may abort on the NEXT unmodeled local prerequisite — exactly the shape wave 16 died of.

RIVAL B — Boot, fire, AND harden the boot so it cannot abort again: recognize that the ladder's LOCAL prerequisites (scratch Repo, full-bundle availability) have failed to line up under one run across MULTIPLE waves (wave 9 aborted 3/4 on full-export-unavailable; wave 16 aborted 6 rungs on scratch-not-booted). Invest in a PRE-ARM checklist that PROVES all of rungs 0-9's local prerequisites green before spending the arm. Virtue: makes the fire near-deterministic. Risk: reads as 'file another instrument', the recession five waves died of.

RIVAL C — Sequence the boot INTO the launcher: the deeper issue is that boot-the-scratch-target is a MANUAL step separate from the launcher, forgotten or mis-homed every wave. Edit pds-crown-launch.sh (NOT frozen — only pds-pull-proof.sh is) so it boots the scratch target into its OWN RUN_TAG-derived home before invoking the harness. Zero new scripts. Virtue: the boot can never be forgotten again. Risk: a launcher edit under time pressure that mis-wires BARKPARK_HOME could strand the very run it means to save.

WHY THE WINNER WON — A executed with B's discipline, C's durability folded in only if the seam demands it. The lead is right that the wave's success condition is THE TRANSCRIPT and that is narrow. But 'boot the scratch target and PROVE scratch.env exists before arming' IS the pre-arm-checklist insight — the lead's own sequence step (1) is literally that. So the winner is Rival A run with a proven (not assumed) pre-arm checklist using the EXISTING instruments, and a launcher-boot integration (C) ONLY if the survey finds the BARKPARK_HOME flow between launcher, scratch-target and harness cannot otherwise be made consistent around the RUN_TAG-derived path. We do not file a fifth instrument; we make the boot a proven precondition of the one shot.

THE SHARPEST ATTACK ON THE WINNER, and how the wave absorbs it: the 'free re-fire' premise may be the very thing that fails the fence — if criterion 11 demands the full bundle be produced UNDER the wave-17 run_id, reusing wave 16's bytes means rungs 3/4 ran against bytes not minted by this run, a hidden mosaic between wave 16's export and wave 17's dev-pull. ABSORPTION: this becomes survey question 2 (read acquire_full_bundle's reuse guard, criterion 11's exact text, and PDS-D236's attribution mechanism). Under D236 attribution is process-level: one process runs all rungs and emits one roster citing the new run_id, and the reuse guard's served_sha == live check IS the D20 freshness proof. So reuse most plausibly satisfies the fence. BUT if the survey finds the fence demands a fresh mint, the wave spends the remaining attempt (budget allows spent+2 = two fires). Re-verifying at fire time and RECORDING reuse-confirmed-or-refused is therefore a hard criterion on the fire slice, not an optimization.

SECOND ATTACK: the scratch boot OOMs or takes 155s cold and the fire slice mistakes it for a hang, or chases it into the frozen harness. ABSORPTION: budget the ~3.5 min cold compile; pre-warm MIX_ENV=prod BEFORE the timed window (PDS-D241) with CC=/usr/bin/clang; redirect boot output to a file, never pipe to tail (PDS-D34 trap 4 hangs forever); local API boot has OOMed before — budget for it, do not mistake an OOM for a hang, do not chase it into the harness. THIRD ATTACK: can ONE --all invocation green rungs 3+4 (full bundle) AND 6 (reboot convergence) AND all dev-pull rungs together? Precedent says yes: wave 7's --all got 10 PASS / 1 FAIL in one process (only rung 6 failed); wave 16's abort was purely the missing scratch.env. Rung 6 is the historically-flaky one and is survey question 4.

The survey plan: 16 Sonnet surveyors, wide net

Width is cheap now; the Digest phase distills. Each question names suspected files, claims to check, and how the answer changes the plan.

1. boot-flow — How BARKPARK_HOME / PDS_SCRATCH_POINTER flow from pds-crown-launch.sh (RUN_ID -> RUN_TAG) into pds-scratch-target.sh up --verify and into pds-pull-proof.sh rung 0c. Does the harness boot the scratch target itself, or expect a pre-booted target in $BARKPARK_HOME? Where must the boot be inserted so scratch.env exists when rung 0c runs? THE load-bearing mechanic — wave 16 aborted here.

2. reuse-fence — Read acquire_full_bundle's served_sha reuse guard, criterion 11's exact text, and PDS-D236's attribution mechanism. Does reusing wave 16's parked bundle under a fresh run_id satisfy 'the run whose full bundle actually existed'? Does the rung 3/4 transcript line cite the run's id on reuse? Load-bearing.

3. bundle-state — Current /tmp/pds-full-export state: attempts file value, budget, full-default.tar.meta served_sha (8eeaf688) vs live guerrilla HEAD RIGHT NOW (SSH + /status.json). If moved, reuse refused -> recompute PDS-D224 spent+2 budget. Is attempts=4, budget=5, one attempt left?

4. rung6-health — On the current sha, is the visibility split still 31 private / 3 public in rung 6's scope, do command/paper/task still declare public, does leg B (PDS_STEP6_GUARD_DEMO=1) fire, what is the Bootstrap SKIP count vs the separate TagRegistry line (PDS-D145)? Wave 7 rung 6 FAILED ('THE CONTROL DID NOT FIRE') and wave 9 PASSED — is it healthy now?

5. launcher-commit — Is pds-crown-launch.sh committed to main / scripts/? It appears only under /private/tmp worktrees, not in scripts/. Where is the canonical copy, are the copies identical, and is editing it (to integrate the boot, Rival C) permitted under the freeze (only pds-pull-proof.sh is frozen)?

6. harness-freeze — Does THIS worktree's scripts/pds-pull-proof.sh match the frozen blob e219e97ccf7f33797c86a2b84d998d599b6bda31 via git rev-parse (never shasum)? Which worktree is suitable to fire from (the primary checkout is UNSUITABLE per PDS-D241)?

7. draw-gate — pds-crown-launch.sh's draw gate: how PDS_LAUNCH_MEM_FLOOR_MIB is read, the build-idle predicate (bp-site-build-* running listing EMPTY, PDS-D227), current MemAvailable + build activity on this host. What value should PDS_LAUNCH_MEM_FLOOR_MIB take to cover 2235.43 MiB while leaving the 2200 harness floor untouched?

8. detached-arm — Exactly how wave 16 armed the launcher detached (nohup/setsid/background), recorded pid + transcript path, and returned without polling. Map the precise invocation and the record format so the fire slice reproduces it. Wave 13 died to agent-turn length with a poller in-turn — the detach is non-negotiable.

9. coldboot-oom — State of api/_build/prod in candidate fire worktrees (ABSENT -> 155.72s prod compile per the wave-13 review). How to pre-warm MIX_ENV=prod with CC=/usr/bin/clang before the timed window. What does an OOM during boot look like vs a hang, and how to not chase it into the harness?

10. mosaic-map — For each of criteria 0-9 on pds-w1-crown-proof, which run_id (if any) does its current evidence cite? Confirm the fence gap: only criterion 0 names a run (20260720T032558Z-28651), and it is stale in substance (deployed sha moved). This is the re-stamp target list.

11. stamp-recipe — Read pds-crown-stamp.sh + pds-crown-stamp-recipe.md. How to re-stamp criteria 0-9 with a fresh run_id, the criterion-11-last-and-alone protocol, the backtick/single-quote escaping traps (criteria 5/6/11), the ~9-11 KB request-line ceiling, and the stale-claim-epoch rejection (bp task pulse bumps the epoch). Note: bp task claim is BROKEN ('unresolved placeholder :doc_id') — claim via HTTP POST /v1/data/mutate/production.

12. autoclose-hazard — cmux_hook.go:193-237: how the false-close fires on a Stop event once every criterion reads met, how criterion 11's presence blocks it, and what the LEAD must watch when stamping 10 so the crown does not close silently on a mosaic.

13. collection-protocol — What exactly does the LEAD do to collect a fire (read transcript, verify the unqualified full-ladder PASS roster, re-stamp 0-9, merge, stamp 10, verify eleven ids, stamp 11)? Map from wave 16's collection task (task-cdff5b4cd01c15d9) and prior collections so the hand-off is unambiguous.

14. prior-papers — Read pds-wave-13-2026-07-21 and any wave 14/15 paper/debrief. What exactly went wrong at each fire attempt (wave 13 agent-turn cut; wave 15 pointed at a probe stub not the real harness; wave 16 scratch-not-booted)? Extract the recurring root cause so wave 17 does not repeat it.

15. concurrent-fence — Are the concurrent cycles (tooling/grip truth-grip w7, cloud/ console-hardening w4, felix-pristine on api/**) touching anything the fire needs, and is the build storm on this host right now going to depress the floor below the tightened gate at fire time? Map the fence collisions and the current bp-site-build-* cadence.

16. migration-parity — Rung 0b asserts guerrilla's deployed sha is an ancestor of the worktree the scratch target migrated from (merge-base --is-ancestor). Current guerrilla deployed sha vs the fire worktree HEAD; will 0b pass at fire time, or is the box ahead of the fire worktree (a PDS-D78 deploy-epoch event, not an assertion to loosen)?

In flight now

Phase: Strategize complete Surveying. 16 Sonnet surveyors dispatched. Next: Digest folds their reports into this Paper and designs the verify fleet BEFORE the verifiers fly. Then Decide appends the wave plan (one boot-and-fire builder slice, opus, plus the seal-naming) BEFORE the builders fly. Then the fire, detached; then the LEAD collects; then Review closes this Paper as the debrief.
description: The crown climb fired for real in wave 16 (1.4 GB export taken, 5 PASS / 0 FAIL) and aborted six rungs on one missing local prerequisite: the scratch target was never booted. Wave 17 boots it, re-fires detached reusing the already-paid bundle, and names the single step to the seal.
